images.title: Creases on a square sheet
images.purpose: Show a square sheet with three pencil lines drawn along its creases, so students ask which pairs meet.
images.composition: One large square sheet centred on a white background with generous margins; the three crease lines sit inside it and the question sits below.
exact_structure: A square sheet with a thin dark outline, about half the frame height.
A teal (#0072B2) horizontal line along the middle crease, from the left edge to the right edge.
An amber (#E69F00) vertical line along the middle crease, from the top edge to the bottom edge, crossing the teal line at the centre.
A reddish purple (#CC79A7) diagonal line from the top left corner to the bottom right corner, passing through the centre.
Exactly 3 lines in total, all passing through the one centre point.
The question text sits centred below the sheet.
rejection: more or fewer than 3 crease lines
the three lines not all passing through the centre
any extra text beyond the question
images.takeaway: Lines drawn on a sheet raise the question of whether two of them meet.
images.description: A square sheet with a horizontal, a vertical and a diagonal crease line crossing at its centre.
images.context: Shown beside the concept text and video for this concept.
images.teaching_notes: Students look at pairs of the three lines and guess which pairs meet.

image_decisions.why: The folded sheet is the hook that raises the question of which lines meet.
